subproblems.title: Graph points are the inverse image of Mathlib's coordinate splitting finAddEquivProd
subproblems.statement: For all natural numbers n, ℓ, all x ∈ ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) and y ∈ ℝ^ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin ℓ): graphPoint x y = E⁻¹(x, y). Here graphPoint x y = toLp 2 (Fin.append (ofLp x) (ofLp y)) is the vector of ℝ^{n+ℓ} = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) whose first n coordinates are x and whose last ℓ coordinates are y, and E = EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd : ℝ^{n+ℓ} ≃L[ℝ] ℝⁿ × ℝ^ℓ is Mathlib's canonical continuous linear equivalence sending z to (its first n coordinates, its last ℓ coordinates).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} (x : Rn n) (y : Rn ℓ), graphPoint x y = (EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd : Amb n ℓ ≃L[ℝ] Rn n × Rn ℓ).symm (x, y)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note: this child is the existing comparator-accepted declaration Submission.rsod_graphPoint_eq_finAddEquivProd_symm (DAG node root.regular_set_open_dense-a1.c1_submanifold_graph_ball-a1.graph_point_linear_equiv-a1, candidate 18a457c495d0ee5b9257b1656886d4da963c6fd8), reused with its byte-identical frozen type. The proof is step 1 of the parent proof (clause (i)), written for one arbitrary pair.

Setup. Fix n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, x ∈ ℝⁿ and y ∈ ℝ^ℓ. Put E := EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd : ℝ^{n+ℓ} ≃L[ℝ] ℝⁿ × ℝ^ℓ (Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/PiL2.lean:378) and G := graphPoint x y = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.append (WithLp.ofLp x) (WithLp.ofLp y)).
1. Coordinates of E. By definition, E is the reindexing LinearIsometryEquiv.piLpCongrLeft 2 ℝ ℝ finSumFinEquiv.symm, followed by EuclideanSpace.sumEquivProd.
- The reindexing maps ℝ^{n+ℓ} to EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n ⊕ Fin ℓ) and sends z to s ↦ z(finSumFinEquiv s).
- sumEquivProd sends a vector indexed by Fin n ⊕ Fin ℓ to the pair (its Sum.inl-part, its Sum.inr-part).
- finSumFinEquiv (Sum.inl i) = Fin.castAdd ℓ i and finSumFinEquiv (Sum.inr j) = Fin.natAdd n j (finSumFinEquiv_apply_left, finSumFinEquiv_apply_right).
Hence, for every z ∈ ℝ^{n+ℓ}, E z = (i ↦ z(Fin.castAdd ℓ i), j ↦ z(Fin.natAdd n j)) ∈ ℝⁿ × ℝ^ℓ.
2. Coordinates of G. For p : Fin (n+ℓ), G(p) = Fin.append (ofLp x) (ofLp y) p (WithLp.ofLp_toLp). So G(Fin.castAdd ℓ i) = x_i for every i : Fin n (Fin.append_left), and G(Fin.natAdd n j) = y_j for every j : Fin ℓ (Fin.append_right).
3. E G = (x, y). Apply step 1 to z = G. The first component of E G has i-th coordinate G(Fin.castAdd ℓ i) = x_i (step 2) for every i : Fin n, so it equals x: Euclidean vectors with equal coordinates are equal (PiLp.ext). Likewise the second component has j-th coordinate G(Fin.natAdd n j) = y_j for every j : Fin ℓ, so it equals y. Hence E G = (x, y) (Prod.ext).
4. Conclusion. E is an equivalence, so E⁻¹(E G) = G (ContinuousLinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply). Therefore graphPoint x y = G = E⁻¹(E G) = E⁻¹(x, y). Since n, ℓ, x, y were arbitrary, the statement holds.
5. Lean outline. This is the accepted proof, recompiled against the pinned Mathlib; it checks the same identity coordinate by coordinate:
intro n ℓ x y; ext i; refine Fin.addCases (fun j => ?_) (fun k => ?_) i; then simp [graphPoint] closes both cases.
In each case simp evaluates the coordinate of E⁻¹(x, y) at Fin.castAdd ℓ j (resp. Fin.natAdd n k) to x_j (resp. y_k), via finSumFinEquiv_symm_apply_castAdd (resp. _natAdd), and the coordinate of graphPoint x y via Fin.append_left (resp. Fin.append_right).
Steps 1 and 3-4 were also compiled literally: for every z, (E z).1 i = z(Fin.castAdd ℓ i) and (E z).2 j = z(Fin.natAdd n j) by simp; E G = (x, y) by Prod.ext and ext + simp [graphPoint]; then rw [← hEG, ContinuousLinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply].
proof_key_steps: E = piLpCongrLeft(finSumFinEquiv.symm) followed by sumEquivProd, so E z = ((z(castAdd ℓ i))_i, (z(natAdd n j))_j)
graphPoint x y has coordinate x_i at castAdd ℓ i and y_j at natAdd n j (Fin.append_left/right)
Hence E(graphPoint x y) = (x, y) componentwise (PiLp.ext, Prod.ext)
Apply E⁻¹: graphPoint x y = E⁻¹(E(graphPoint x y)) = E⁻¹(x, y)

subproblems.title: Pythagorean identity for graph points
subproblems.statement: For all natural numbers n, ℓ, all x ∈ ℝⁿ and y ∈ ℝ^ℓ (the Euclidean spaces EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) and EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin ℓ) with their Euclidean norms), the graph point graphPoint x y = toLp 2 (Fin.append (ofLp x) (ofLp y)) ∈ ℝ^{n+ℓ} (first n coordinates x, last ℓ coordinates y) satisfies ‖graphPoint x y‖² = ‖x‖² + ‖y‖².
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} (x : Rn n) (y : Rn ℓ), ‖graphPoint x y‖ ^ 2 = ‖x‖ ^ 2 + ‖y‖ ^ 2
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note: this child is the existing comparator-accepted declaration Submission.rsod_norm_graphPoint_sq (DAG node root.regular_set_open_dense-a1.c1_submanifold_graph_ball-a1.norm_graph_point_sq-a1, candidate a2b4772332bc9c27da8217e3494b043a4d2dec4c), reused with its byte-identical frozen type. The proof is step 3 of the parent proof (clause (ii)). The coordinates of graphPoint are read directly from its definition, so this child does not depend on the other child.

Setup. Fix n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, x ∈ ℝⁿ and y ∈ ℝ^ℓ, and put G := graphPoint x y = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.append (WithLp.ofLp x) (WithLp.ofLp y)) ∈ ℝ^{n+ℓ}.
1. Norms as sums of squares. For a finite index type ι and z ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ ι, ‖z‖² = Σ_{p : ι} z_p² (EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq, PiL2.lean:153; equivalently EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq with ‖t‖² = t² for real t). Hence ‖G‖² = Σ_{p : Fin (n+ℓ)} G_p², ‖x‖² = Σ_{i : Fin n} x_i² and ‖y‖² = Σ_{j : Fin ℓ} y_j².
2. Coordinates of G. G_p = Fin.append (ofLp x) (ofLp y) p for each p : Fin (n+ℓ) (WithLp.ofLp_toLp). So G_{Fin.castAdd ℓ i} = x_i for i : Fin n (Fin.append_left), and G_{Fin.natAdd n j} = y_j for j : Fin ℓ (Fin.append_right).
3. Splitting the index set. For every f : Fin (n+ℓ) → ℝ, Σ_{p : Fin (n+ℓ)} f p = Σ_{i : Fin n} f(Fin.castAdd ℓ i) + Σ_{j : Fin ℓ} f(Fin.natAdd n j) (Fin.sum_univ_add). Take f p := G_p² and use step 2: Σ_p G_p² = Σ_i x_i² + Σ_j y_j².
4. Conclusion. By steps 1 and 3, ‖G‖² = Σ_i x_i² + Σ_j y_j² = ‖x‖² + ‖y‖², i.e. ‖graphPoint x y‖² = ‖x‖² + ‖y‖². Since n, ℓ, x, y were arbitrary, the statement holds.
5. Lean outline (the accepted proof, recompiled against the pinned Mathlib): intro n ℓ x y; rw [EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq, EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq, EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq, Fin.sum_univ_add]; simp [graphPoint].
proof_key_steps: ‖z‖² = Σ_p z_p² for real Euclidean vectors (EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq)
Coordinates of graphPoint x y: castAdd ℓ i ↦ x_i and natAdd n j ↦ y_j (Fin.append_left/right)
Split the sum over Fin (n+ℓ) with Fin.sum_univ_add
Recombine the two partial sums into ‖x‖² + ‖y‖²
